content.text: The verifier's substantive review affirms every element of the finding — status, cited paragraphs, direction analysis, the minimal-edit decision, and the explanation of the false-signal check. There is no defect to repair: the only "failed" item is the deterministic frequency-cap regex, which cannot match where no audit clause exists, and that is already explained rather than ignored. I am re-submitting the compliant finding unchanged in substance, with no redline.

input.quote: Contractor shall bill Company as set forth in the relevant Statement of Work. Each invoice submitted by Contractor will provide supporting detail for the Services invoiced, including, to the extent applicable to a particular engagement, the dates of Services and hours worked at the applicable rate by Statement of Work.
input.rationale: No audit, inspection, verification or monitoring right runs against Clear Capital anywhere in the agreement. A document-wide regex sweep for "audit|inspect|verif|examin|monitor|books and records|compliance review" returns zero matches, and the sections flagged by the planner contain no such right: § 3 governs compensation and invoicing, § 4 governs ownership and acceptance of Works. Both candidate paragraphs run in our favour rather than against us: p0014 (§ 3) obliges Contractor to supply invoice supporting detail, dates, hours worked and expense receipts to us, and p0007(ii) (§ 1) requires Contractor to observe Company's rules on access to and security of Company computer systems — a restriction on the counterparty, not a grant of access to our systems. Because AUDIT constrains a Vendor-favourable right and no such right exists here, there is nothing exceeding the limits on frequency, notice, cost allocation or system access, so no redline or comment is warranted. Inserting frequency/notice/cost limits would gratuitously create a Vendor audit right that the current bargain omits, contrary to the minimal-edit principle. The failed deterministic check "audit frequency limited" is a false signal: the regex cannot match a frequency cap because there is no audit clause to cap, and the apparent frequency hits are incidental substrings inside ordinary words ("concerning", "concepts"). Residual risk to monitor: a future Statement of Work could introduce an audit or usage-verification right, in which case the preferred position applies — once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Contractor-borne cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no direct access to our systems.
